{{Short description|British mathematician}}
[[File:Henry William Watson.jpg|thumb|Henry William Watson]]

{{Use dmy dates|date=October 2019}}
Rev. '''Henry William Watson''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]] (25 February 1827, [[Marylebone]], [[London]]{{spaced ndash}}11 January 1903, [[Brighton]]) was a mathematician and author of a number of mathematics books. He was an ordained [[priest]] and [[Cambridge Apostle]].

==Life==
Watson was born at [[Marylebone]] to Thomas Watson, R.N., and Eleanor Mary Kingston.<ref name="dnb">{{DNB12|wstitle=Watson, Henry William|first=T. E.|last= James}}</ref>

He was educated at [[King's College London]] and at [[Trinity College, Cambridge]].<ref>{{acad|id=WT846HW|name=Watson, Henry William}}</ref> He graduated as second [[Wrangler (University of Cambridge)|wrangler]] and Smith's prizeman in 1850, Dr. [[W. H. Besant]] being senior wrangler. 
In 1851 he became fellow of Trinity college, and from 1851 to 1853 was assistant tutor there. Watson formed a close friendship with [[James Fitzjames Stephen]], who entered Trinity in 1847.<ref name="dnb"/> From 1853 he was mathematical master in the City of London School, and in 1857 he became mathematical lecturer at King′s College.

Watson was ordained [[deacon]] in 1856, and two years later received priest′s orders. He was an assistant master at [[Harrow School]] from 1857 to 1865, when he became [[Rector (ecclesiastical)|rector]] of [[Berkswell]] near [[Coventry]]. He kept this position for 37 years, resigning in August 1902, when he moved to Brighton. His time at the rectory provided ample time to pursue mathematical and scientific studies, and he was a frequent contributor to scientific literature.<ref name=TTobit />

He and [[Francis Galton]] introduced the [[Galton&ndash;Watson process]] in 1875. He was made a Fellow of the [[Royal Society]] (FRS) in 1881, and took the degree [[Doctor of Science|D.Sc.]] in 1883.

He died in Brighton on 11 January 1903.<ref name=TTobit>{{Cite newspaper The Times |title=Obituary - Rev. Henry W. Watson |date=13 January 1903 |page=7 |issue=36976}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Watson married Emily Rowe in 1856. They had three children, one son and two daughters.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Henry Watson - Biography |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Watson_Henry/ |access-date=2025-09-15 |website=Maths History |language=en}}</ref>

==Books by H. W. Watson==
* [https://archive.org/details/mathematicaltheo01watsrich The mathematical theory of electricity and magnetism (Volume 1: electrostatics)] (Clarendon, Oxford, 1885&ndash;1889) 
* [https://archive.org/details/mathematicaltheo02watsrich The mathematical theory of electricity and magnetism (Volume 2: magnetism & electrodynamics)] (Clarendon, Oxford, 1885&ndash;1889)
* [https://archive.org/details/Aplicationofgene00watsrich A treatise on the application of generalised coordinates to the kinetics of a material system] (Clarendon, Oxford, 1879) 
* [https://archive.org/details/treatiseonkineti00watsiala A treatise on the kinetic theory of gases] (Clarendon, Oxford, 1893)
